call.x: Apply for funding to undertake a large team-based curiosity-driven bioscience discovery research project. You must be based at a UK research organisation eligible for BBSRC funding. Full stage submissions are invitation only following assessment of an sLoLa outline application.
n: Run by Biotechnology and Biological Sciences Research Council (BBSRC). The organiser sets the rules; Eligible Calls reads this call from UKRI Funding Finder (ukri.org).

UKRI-2026-to-2027-strategic-longer-and-l.heading: How we will assess your application

blocks.text: Assessment process
We will assess your application using the following process.
Full stage will only be open to successful applicants who have been invited to submit following the assessment of their outline application.
Expert review
We will invite experts to review your application independently, against the specified criteria for this funding opportunity.
You will not be able to nominate reviewers for applications on the new UK Research and Innovation (UKRI) Funding Service. Research councils will continue to select expert reviewers.
We are monitoring the requirement for applicant-nominated reviewers as we review policies and processes as part of the continued development of the new Funding Service.
You will have 14 days to respond to reviewers’ comments.
Full stage panel

Following expert review, we will invite experts to use the evidence provided by reviewers and your applicant response to assess the quality of your application. The multidisciplinary panel comprises of outline stage Strategic longer and larger committee (SLC) members and further subject matter experts, including representatives from BBSRC’s responsive mode research committees and BBSRC’s pool of experts.

Following assessment, the committee will provide feedback and recommendations to Biotechnology and Biological Sciences Research Council (BBSRC) of highly rated applications to be considered for funding.
We expect the full stage panel process to take place in May to early June 2027.

Where applications are closely competitive, the Strategic Leadership Committee (SLC) may conduct interviews to support final funding decisions. Interviews will typically involve the project lead and up to three other core team members. Further details will be provided to shortlisted teams in this case.
BBSRC will make the final funding decision.
For more information on how we prioritise applications for funding please visit How we make decisions .
Feedback

BBSRC will not provide additional feedback for all applications following the communication of the outcomes of the applications. Peer review comments will serve as the source of feedback for applicants.
Principles of assessment
We support the San Francisco declaration on research assessment and recognise the relationship between research assessment and research integrity.
Find out about the UKRI principles of assessment and decision making .
Using generative artificial intelligence (AI) in expert review

Generative AI may only be used for the purpose of language refinement during application assessment. When using generative AI to refine the language of a review, expert reviewers and panellists must ensure that:
no part of the application being assessed is entered into a generative AI tool
no personal information from the application is disclosed
generative AI is not tasked with understanding, summarising or evaluating the application’s content
Expert reviewers and panellists must also:
comply with relevant intellectual property and data protection legislation
not take into account or speculate within their assessment whether generative AI has been used to develop the application
For more detail see our policy on the use of generative AI .
We reserve the right to modify the assessment process as needed.
Assessment areas
The assessment areas we will use are:
vision
approach
applicant and team capability to deliver
resources and cost justification
ethics and responsible research and innovation (RRI)
strategic case
management strategy
team culture and development

The addition of the team culture and development assessment area aligns with the goals of the UKRI people and teams assessment pilot . Assessors are asked to consider if the people and teams aspects of applications are described adequately and align with the team science approach that underpins the sLoLa scheme. Given the multidisciplinary nature of sLoLa awards, there are enhanced opportunities to support the development of team members, foster inclusive and collaborative working practices, and promote a positive research culture across the wider team.
Find details of assessment questions and criteria under the ‘Application questions’ heading in the ‘How to apply’ section.

HE-GA-B.title: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026-2027, General Annexes, B - Eligibility

consortium.quote: Unless otherwise provided for in the specific call/topic conditions, only legal entities forming a consortium are eligible to participate in actions provided that the consortium includes, as beneficiaries, three legal entities independent from each other and each established in a different country as follows: – at least one independent legal entity established in a Member State; and – at least two other independent legal entities, each established in different Member States or Associated Countries.
